bug_semantics: The login page pre-fills the username field from an unauthenticated, attacker-controlled request parameter and stores it in the template context without HTML-encoding: Login() assigns $context['default_username'] = &$_REQUEST['u'] (a by-reference assignment from the raw request). The login template later echoes default_username into the value attribute of the username input, so a crafted link like index.php?action=login&u="><script>... executes arbitrary web script or HTML in the SMF origin (persistent context XSS, CWE-20 improper input validation per the advisory).
flaw_origin: Commit a18e888838460a816fdbc2703e7e05ce7f626c91 (2012-01-24, author Spuds, message "10610" — an SVN-to-git conversion revision) first added to Sources/LogInOut.php the line `$context['default_username'] = &$_REQUEST['u'];` (by-reference from raw request, no htmlspecialchars, unlike the sibling POST-based assignments at lines 247/284 of the same file which do escape). A scoped `git log -S 'default_username' -- Sources/LogInOut.php` shows the sequence a18e8888 (2012, introduction), 26d5efdf (2014, trim), a9e979d2 (2023, file move to Actions/Login2.php), then the 2026 fixes — the vulnerable assignment was written once in a18e8888 and never encoded until the fix. The 2023 move a9e979d2e718304c8de23dfb637074f6774d174b is a relocation boundary, not the origin. The commit is the root commit of the converted history (no parent object), so introducer_parent is null and introducer_parent_absent is justified by the parent-tree check showing zero occurrences of the by-reference assignment before this commit.
